subject: Vendor evaluation: gating matrix + SLA qualification for HoloHealth MAP
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Amita Sharma <amita@holohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft gating matrix + SLA qualification (MAP kickoff)

Amita — great to meet last week. Per our call, I put together an initial vendor evaluation gating matrix and a proposed SLA qualification checklist so we can align MAP milestones to decision gates. Attached is a simple workbook with three tabs: SuccessSignals, ExitGates, and AcceptanceTests.

Top-level asks for this thread:
- Please confirm the functional success signals you care most about (latency, throughput, semantic accuracy on your eval prompts).
- Call out any non-negotiable security/compliance checks (SOC2, VPC peering, KMS) we should include as hard exit gates.
- Can procurement suggest a target window for contract review (we usually need ~7 business days for minor redlines)?

Highlights from our side:
- 90p latency goal: <= 350ms for 512-token prompts under production load (we propose this as a gate).
- Throughput: target baseline of 100 rps with 95% availability in the Dedicated pilot.
- Quality: accuracy threshold defined via your 120-case eval set (we'll run and share metrics).

Attachments: [HoloHealth-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)], [Redwood-SLA-Draft-v2.pdf (pdf)]

Next steps: if you confirm the priority signals I’ll route the workbook to Rishi for technical acceptance criteria and to Marissa for commercial timeline alignment.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Amita Sharma <amita@holohealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: HoloHealth Procurement <procurement@holohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft gating matrix + SLA qualification (MAP kickoff)

Thanks, Kimberly — this is helpful and lines up with what leadership wants to see in a pilot MAP. Quick answers:
- Priority success signals: 1) semantic accuracy on our 120-case clinical-safety set (we'll share the spreadsheet), 2) mean latency under load (50–95p bands), 3) audit log completeness for every request.
- Security: SOC2 report and evidence of encrypted-at-rest keys (KMS/HSM) are required before production pilot. VPC peering is preferred but we can accept an isolated private deployment if peering takes longer.
- Procurement: target window is 10 business days for initial redlines; can compress if both sides agree in advance.

I'll upload our eval prompts and the clinical-safety scoring rubric this afternoon. Looking forward to Rishi's technical acceptance tests.

—Amita
Amita Sharma
Director of Product, HoloHealth
amita@holohealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Amita Sharma <amita@holohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft gating matrix + SLA qualification (MAP kickoff)

Amita / Kimberly — I reviewed the gating matrix and sketched technical acceptance tests in the attached markdown. High-level proposals (we can iterate):

1) Performance gates (acceptance tests):
- Latency: 90th percentile end-to-end <= 350ms for 512-token prompts under a sustained 100 rps synthetic workload that mirrors your QPS distribution. Test harness: our internal load generator + your sample trace.
- Throughput: sustain 100 rps for 30 minutes without KV cache misses > 5% (we'll define cache warmup).
- Stability: no more than 1 transient error spike >1% of requests during a 24-hour soak.

2) Quality gates (acceptance tests):
- Accuracy: pass rate >= 88% on your 120-case clinical-safety eval when scored against your rubric (we'll produce detailed diffs).
- Regression: no more than a 3-point drop on F1/accuracy metrics compared to the baseline run.

3) Security/compliance gates:
- SOC2 Type II report or equivalent + signed attestation for data handling.
- KMS-based key management for customer-owned keys (workspace-level KMS integration).

4) Operational gates:
- Audit logs: per-request trace and payer id exported to your secure bucket with <10s delivery latency.
- Rollback policy: automatic fallback to a smaller-capacity model with identical API surface on degraded performance.

Attachment referenced: [acceptance-test-cases.md (text)] — includes test commands, expected outputs, and pass/fail threshold examples.

If these look good, I'll convert acceptance-test-cases.md into runnable test jobs and share step-by-step runbooks.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amita Sharma <amita@holohealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft gating matrix + SLA qualification (MAP kickoff)

Amita — adding a commercial/timeline view to the MAP so procurement has what they need.

Proposed close timeline for pilot + contract:
- Week 0 (sign MAP): kickoff + access to eval prompts and access plan.
- Week 1–2: run initial acceptance tests (Rishi executes).
- Week 3: joint review of results; if gates met, we enable Dedicated pilot environment.
- Week 4–6: pilot run and operational validation.
- Contract: draft SLA circulated by Redwood Day 3 of MAP; procurement redlines due by Day 10.

Commercial notes:
- We propose a 3-month Pilot credit allowance with price protection for first paid term if pilot achieves gates.
- If SOC2 evidence requires time, we can start an isolated test environment with strict data handling (no PHI ingestion) until attestation is complete.

Attachment: [Redwood-SLA-Draft-v2.pdf] — contains our standard latency/uptime commitments and proposed liability language.

Let me know if 10 business days from SLA first delivery is workable for procurement.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, GTM Programs, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

- For the accuracy gate, we'll anonymize/scrub PHI and deliver the 120-case set by EOD today.
- Procurement: 10 business days for SLA review is acceptable. Procurement will start a parallel review once Marissa uploads the DocuSign draft.

If those three items are confirmable, we’re ready to sign the MAP and start test runs next Monday.

—Amita
